description: Doubledecker on channel 1 plays a four-chord progression, C, A minor, F and G in C major, on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 of every bar for four bars at 90 BPM, as triads at velocity 80 with Chd1 on the 3rd and Chd2 on the 5th, each chord two steps long. In bar 1 the chords are blocks, all three notes together. In bars 2 and 3 Chord Strum 1 is locked on each chord step with Spread 1 and Acceleration minus 1, so the root sounds first, the 3rd two steps later and the 5th a step after that, a strum that speeds up, about half a second end to end. In bar 4 Chord Arp 1/2 is locked on as well and takes over from the strum, so each chord becomes just two short notes, the root and then the 3rd a step and a half later. Listen for the chords opening up into a quickening strum at bar 2, about 2.7 seconds in, and for the strum turning into a sparse, detached two-note figure at bar 4, about 8 seconds in.
synchronization: Observed framebuffer/grid sampled against host monotonic recording time; not sample-exact or physical-norns calibration.
title: Block chords, strummed, then arpeggiated
